Engineering Note: Alerting on Database Saturation

The Job Event Store, our document database for field technician activity, has degraded twice under load without warning us first, so we built dedicated alerting around it before this quarter's dispatch-volume growth.

The Job Event Store Resource is the monitored resource record for the whole deployment: it monitors the Field Ops Compute Cluster, the compute node the database runs on, and the DocumentDB Engine, the system software running on that node. Everything we measure about the database's health is scoped to that one resource.

The Connection Pool Saturation Gauge is the metric instrument that actually tracks how many of the database's available connections are in use at any moment, and it monitors the Job Event Store directly. That gauge depends on the Job Event Store Resource -- without the resource record, the gauge would have no scope to attach its measurements to. The gauge satisfies a specific requirement: Connection Pool Saturation Must Be Visible Before It Causes Request Failures, which is exactly the gap that burned us during the two prior incidents.

We watch that gauge with the Connection Pool Saturation Alert, an alerting rule that monitors the Connection Pool Saturation Gauge and fires the moment utilization crosses eighty percent, well before the pool actually exhausts. That alert feeds the Database Health Dashboard, the monitoring dashboard the on-call engineer opens first during any dispatch-volume incident; the dashboard monitors both the Connection Pool Saturation Alert and the Connection Pool Saturation Gauge directly, so the on-call engineer can see the raw trend line next to the alert state in one place.
